components.name: Graded Slab
components.description: An achievement sealed in clear acrylic with a printed grade label, lifting out of its slot on hover.
components.css: .ds-slab { width: 62px; height: 88px; padding: 4px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; border-radius: 5px; background: linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(255,255,255,.38), rgba(255,255,255,.1) 38%, rgba(255,255,255,.04) 62%, rgba(255,255,255,.16)), rgba(18,22,28,.22); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.45), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.85), 0 6px 10px -3px rgba(0,0,0,.5); transition: transform .28s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-slab:hover { transform: translateY(-8px); } .ds-grade { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 22px; border-radius: 2px; overflow: hidden; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; text-align: center; color: #16181b; line-height: 1; } .ds-grade-tier { flex: 1; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #c79bff; font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; letter-spacing: .05em; } .ds-grade-pct { flex: 1; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #f4f2ec; font-weight: 600; font-size: 10px; } .ds-insert { width: 54px; height: 54px; border-radius: 2px; background: #0d1014; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.8); }

components.name: Display Rail
components.description: Matte black anodised rail with a slot channel; the trophy variant adds a brass front edge.
components.css: .ds-rail { position: relative; width: 300px; height: 12px; border-radius: 3px; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, #34383e 0 1px, #23262a 1px 4px, #17191c 4px calc(100% - 2px), #0a0b0d calc(100% - 2px)); box-shadow: 0 5px 9px -2px rgba(0,0,0,.55); } .ds-rail::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 1px; left: 14px; right: 14px; height: 3px; border-radius: 1px; background: #050506; }

narrative.overview:
Every achievement is a graded collectible. It's sealed in a clear acrylic slab with a printed grade label, and stands in a matte black display rail fixed to the bottom-right of the user's desktop. The user's own wallpaper is the ground, seen through the acrylic. The system is made of three real materials (clear acrylic, black anodised rail, off-white card stock) plus the printed rarity colour. Nothing glows and nothing is decoration. The grade label is the one place colour appears, so rarity is the first thing the eye reads.

The widget is on screen all day over unknown wallpaper, so every surface has to hold up over both light and dark backgrounds, and it stays still unless the user touches it.
keyCharacteristics: Clear acrylic slabs, 62×88, each with a two-tone grade label and a dark icon insert.
Matte black rails with a slot channel; the slab's foot sits down in the slot.
Off-white card stock for every printed surface: grade labels and placards. The tooltip certificate is cut from the rail's black anodised stock, with its grade printed on card stock.
Colour comes only from the five rarity tiers.
Motion only happens when the user acts or something changes: lift on hover, a drop into the slot for new unlocks.

rules.name: The Printed Colour Rule
rules.body: Rarity colour appears only as printed ink on a grade label: never as glow, border tint, or background wash.

rules.name: The Ungraded Rule
rules.body: An achievement with no known rarity gets an unprinted tier block (card stock with muted "Ungraded" text). It never borrows a tier colour.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: The certificate opens with the title. The game name goes under it as a plain meta line, never as a small tracked caps label above it.

dos: Do keep colour to the printed rarity tiers. Every other surface is acrylic, black rail, brass, or card stock.
Do put any text that sits over the wallpaper on card stock.
Do make every motion answer a user action or a change: hover lift, new-unlock drop, legendary glare.
donts: Don't loop any animation; the widget is on screen all day.
Don't use glows, neon edges, or glassy blur. `backdrop-filter` can't see the desktop through the transparent window anyway.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons.
Don't put an eyebrow label above a heading.
